newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler May U.S. vehicle sales drop 16.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler May U.S. vehicle sales drop 16.6 percent.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said on Monday its U.S. light vehicle sales in May dropped 16.6 percent from a year-earlier record as consumer demand softened and an engine plant strike curtailed truck and Jeep production.
Chrysler said it sold 204,654 cars and trucks last month, compared with an all-time high of 245,289 in May 1996.
Chrysler's passenger car sales fell 17.9 percent from a year ago to 72,944 units, while truck sales, normally a source of strength for Chrysler, slid 15.5 percent to 131,710 units.

"The spring market is significantly softer than a year ago -- when we were setting all-time sales records in most categories -- and competition is fierce," James Holden, Chrysler's executive vice president of sales and marketing, said in a statement accompanying the results.
"But consumers are confident, interest rates are reasonable and our products continue to be outstanding values."
Chrysler sold 23,852 Dodge Ram Pickup trucks, down about 36 percent from May 1996 and down 22 percent from April 1997.

Chrysler halted production of the Ram and four other truck models during a month-long strike at its Mound Road Engine Plant in Detroit that ended May 9. The strike cut off supplies of the automaker's V-8 and V-6 truck engines.

May sales of Chrysler's Jeep Grand Cherokee were off 16 percent from a year ago and Ram van sales slid 69 percent. Dodge Dakota pickup sales rose 18 percent over year-ago sales of the previous-generation model, but fell 15 percent from April.
In addition, Chrysler said sales of other vehicles not affected by the strike were down. Sales of its redesigned Cherokee fell 7 percent from year-ago levels, and minivan sales were down 6 percent.

All of Chrysler's passenger car models showed declines except for the Dodge Stratus, which registered an 8 percent increase over year-ago levels. Stratus sales in May included significant deliveries to rental fleets, a Chrysler spokesman said.
Analysts expect General Motors Corp. also to report a May sales decline on Tuesday, and Ford Motor Co. to report lower sales on Wednesday.
Chrysler's stock fell 37.5 cents to $32.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
